samples.summary: Non-finite geometry from collaborator-controlled document data can now propagate into x/y
samples.evidence: `anchoredFramePatch` derives x/y from `resizeFrameToSize(frame, …)`, which multiplies by `Math.cos(start.rotation)` / `Math.sin(start.rotation)` (packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/resize.ts:145-158). Panel input itself is validated finite (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/format-panel/size-position-section.tsx:273,316), but `frame.rotation`/`frame.w`/`frame.h` come from the shared Yorkie document, and `YorkieSlidesStore.updateElementFrame` writes the patch with no numeric validation (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:1456). A malicious/buggy collaborator who writes a non-finite or absurd `rotation` into the CRDT makes a subsequent local W/H commit persist NaN `x`/`y` for every peer, where previously a size-only patch left x/y intact. Integrity/availability of the shared doc only — no auth, secret, or injection impact; I could not confirm a peer can actually write a non-finite rotation, hence low confidence.

samples.summary: No authorization, secret, injection, crypto, SSRF, deserialization or path-traversal surface is touched by this change
samples.evidence: The change is pure client-side geometry: a new pure exported function `resizeFrameToSize` (refactor of existing `frameAtAnchor` math), a 5-line frontend helper, and its wiring into two existing `store.updateElementFrame` call sites in FormatPanel. I enumerated the other callers of the affected operation (`updateElementFrame`: packages/slides/src/view/editor/{editor.ts,interactions/{drag,keyboard}.ts}, store/memory.ts, store/layout-edit-store.ts:96, yorkie-slides-store.ts:1430, yorkie-board-store.ts:670) — none of them gain a new unguarded path from this diff, and the write-permission gate that governs FormatPanel is unchanged: it is only mountable behind `!readOnly` derived from `resolved.role === "viewer"` (packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:431,500-543,626-686). No credentials, tokens, exec/SQL/path sinks, or signature checks appear in the diff, and the added docs/test/task files contain no instruction-injection text.
